intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the gene encoding thrombopoietin (THPO; 600044) on chromosome 3q27.1.

checks.claim: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the THPO gene, which encodes thrombopoietin.
checks.evidence_quote: In conclusion, mutations of the THPO gene cause a form of CAMT that can be treated with THPO‐receptor agonists.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous THPO p.R119C as the cause of CAMT. The CAMT2 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The THPO gene is located on chromosome 3q27.1.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome and targeted sequencing identified mutations in the gene encoding thrombopoietin (THPO)
checks.explanation: The 3q27.1 location is standard nomenclature, so it counts as supported even though the abstract does not state it.

paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive bone marrow failure disorder. It begins with thrombocytopenia and a lack of megakaryocytes and can progress to pancytopenia and aplastic anemia (Pecci et al., 2018). Dasouki et al. (2013) attributed the disorder to loss of function of thrombopoietin, the ligand of the MPL receptor. Pecci et al. (2018) noted that thrombopoietin is mainly made in the liver, so hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is not expected to correct the defect, and patients have responded to the thrombopoietin receptor agonist romiplostim.

checks.claim: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive bone marrow failure disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is shown in the family, and the paper describes the disorder as bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: CAMT2 begins with thrombocytopenia and a lack of megakaryocytes.
checks.evidence_quote: inherited disorder characterized at birth by thrombocytopenia with reduced megakaryocytes, which evolves into generalized bone marrow aplasia during childhood
checks.explanation: The disorder starts at birth with thrombocytopenia and reduced megakaryocytes.

checks.claim: CAMT2 can progress to pancytopenia and aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: subsequently evolution, usually within the first decade of life, into pancytopenia due to trilineage bone marrow aplasia
checks.explanation: The paper describes progression to pancytopenia and marrow aplasia.

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. (2013) attributed CAMT2 to loss of function of thrombopoietin.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, the R17C partial loss-of-function allele results in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state in our family.
checks.explanation: The paper links the disorder to a partial loss-of-function THPO allele. It calls the disorder aplastic anemia, not CAMT2, and says 'partial' loss of function.

checks.claim: Thrombopoietin is the ligand of the MPL receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: Together with the recent identification of THPO receptor (MPL) mutations
checks.explanation: The abstract identifies MPL as the THPO receptor.

checks.claim: Thrombopoietin is mainly produced in the liver.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the paper.

checks.claim: Because thrombopoietin is mainly produced in the liver, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is not expected to correct the defect in CAMT2.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells, these patients are not expected to benefit from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the paper.

checks.claim: Patients with CAMT2 have responded to the thrombopoietin receptor agonist romiplostim.
checks.evidence_quote: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence
checks.explanation: All three patients responded to romiplostim.

paragraphs.text: Dasouki et al. (2013) described 2 sibs from a Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. (2013) described 2 sibs from a Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently identified 2 siblings afflicted with idiopathic, autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.explanation: The Micronesian family is named in the title, and the 2 affected siblings are described in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) reported patients with inherited bone marrow failure caused by THPO mutations. Their bone marrow failure did not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, but blood counts improved with thrombopoietin receptor agonist treatment.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) reported patients with inherited bone marrow failure caused by THPO mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We report 5 individuals in 3 unrelated families with severe thrombocytopenia progressing to trilineage bone marrow failure (BMF).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes familial cases with homozygous THPO mutations causing bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: The bone marrow failure in the patients with THPO mutations reported by Seo et al. (2017) did not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
checks.evidence_quote: Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants and all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states this.

checks.claim: Blood counts in the patients with THPO mutations reported by Seo et al. (2017) improved with thrombopoietin receptor agonist treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: For the 2 surviving patients, improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis was achieved following treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states this.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported a family with 3 children who had congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia caused by a homozygous THPO mutation. Treatment with romiplostim was effective in all 3 affected children.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) reported a family with 3 children who had congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a family with three children affected with CAMT caused by a homozygous mutation (p.R119C) of the THPO gene.
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia in the 3 children reported by Pecci et al. (2018) was caused by a homozygous THPO mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a family with three children affected with CAMT caused by a homozygous mutation (p.R119C) of the THPO gene.
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: Romiplostim treatment was effective in all 3 affected children reported by Pecci et al. (2018).
checks.evidence_quote: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CAMT2 in the family reported by Dasouki et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Recessive inheritance was also seen in the family reported by Pecci et al. (2018), in which the affected sibs were homozygous and the parents heterozygous for the THPO mutation.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of CAMT2 in the family reported by Dasouki et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: the R17C partial loss-of-function allele results in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state in our family
checks.explanation: The affected siblings are homozygous and the parents heterozygous, and the paper calls the disorder autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Recessive inheritance of CAMT2 was seen in the family reported by Pecci et al. (2018).
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the paper.

checks.claim: In the family reported by Pecci et al. (2018), the affected sibs were homozygous for the THPO mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified the homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C). Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous
checks.explanation: The proband and both siblings were homozygous.

checks.claim: In the family reported by Pecci et al. (2018), the parents were heterozygous for the THPO mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) noted that congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-1 (CAMT1) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the thrombopoietin receptor (MPL).

checks.claim: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-1 (CAMT1) is caused by mutation in the MPL gene, which encodes the thrombopoietin receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: The majority of CAMT cases are caused by biallelic mutations in the gene (MPL) encoding for the myeloproliferative leukemia virus oncogene (MPL) receptor
checks.explanation: MPL is described as the thrombopoietin receptor gene that causes most CAMT. The CAMT1 label is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a Micronesian family with aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.112C-T missense mutation in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution (R17C when the 21-amino acid signal peptide is excluded).

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. (2013) used whole-exome sequencing in 2 sibs from a Micronesian family with aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: Whole-exome sequencing was used in the 2 affected siblings.

checks.claim: The 2 Micronesian sibs with aplastic anemia reported by Dasouki et al. (2013) were homozygous for a c.112C-T missense mutation in the THPO gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: The variant, the zygosity and the number of affected siblings all match.

checks.claim: The THPO c.112C-T mutation results in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation encodes an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38
checks.explanation: The paper states the substitution is arginine to cysteine at residue 38 (R38C).

checks.claim: The THPO R38C substitution is designated R17C when the 21-amino acid signal peptide is excluded.
checks.evidence_quote: an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38 or residue 17 excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide
checks.explanation: The paper gives the R17C numbering for when the 21-amino-acid signal peptide is excluded.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) identified homozygous THPO mutations, including R99W, in patients with bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) identified homozygous THPO mutations in patients with bone marrow failure.
checks.evidence_quote: THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families, and THPO R157X, homozygous in the affected child in the third family.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states this.

checks.claim: The homozygous THPO mutations identified by Seo et al. (2017) in patients with bone marrow failure included R99W.
checks.evidence_quote: THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states this.

paragraphs.text: In patients with CAMT, Pecci et al. (2018) identified a homozygous c.355C-T missense mutation in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution. The patients responded to romiplostim.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) identified a homozygous c.355C-T missense mutation in the THPO gene in patients with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.
checks.evidence_quote: While no variants were found in MPL, we identified the homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C).
checks.explanation: Matches the Results section. The Methods section writes the mutagenesis construct as c.335C>T, which looks like a typo. Codon 119 begins at nucleotide 355, so c.355 is consistent.

checks.claim: The THPO c.355C-T mutation results in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified the homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C)
checks.explanation: R119C is the same as arg119-to-cys.

checks.claim: The patients with the homozygous THPO R119C mutation reported by Pecci et al. (2018) responded to romiplostim.
checks.evidence_quote: romiplostim was effective in increasing platelet count in all our patients, as well as in increasing hemoglobin concentration and neutrophil count in subjects presenting with anemia and/or neutropenia
checks.explanation: All patients responded to romiplostim.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) found that the thrombopoietin receptor agonist romiplostim improved hematopoiesis in their patients with THPO mutations and in patients reported by Seo et al. (2017). Seo et al. (2017) found that hematopoietic stem cell transplantation did not correct the defect in patients with THPO mutations. Pecci et al. (2018) explained this by the fact that thrombopoietin is produced outside the hematopoietic cells.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) found that the thrombopoietin receptor agonist romiplostim improved hematopoiesis in their patients with THPO mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses
checks.explanation: Trilineage responses in all three patients.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) found that romiplostim improved hematopoiesis in the patients with THPO mutations reported by Seo et al. (2017).
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with our observations, trilineage response to romiplostim was achieved by two affected individuals homozygous for the p.R99W or p.R157* mutations of THPO (Seo et al, 2017).
checks.explanation: Pecci et al. only cite Seo et al.'s results. They did not find this themselves, and the response was in two of Seo's patients, not all of them.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) found that hematopoietic stem cell transplantation did not correct the defect in patients with THPO mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants and all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that transplantation failed to correct the cytopenias.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) attributed the failure of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in patients with THPO mutations to thrombopoietin being produced outside hematopoietic cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells, these patients are not expected to benefit from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
checks.explanation: The paper explains that HSCT would not help because thrombopoietin is produced outside hematopoietic cells.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Reduced or absent bone marrow megakaryocytes

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.112C-T transition in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution (R17C when the 21-amino acid signal peptide is excluded).

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. (2013) used whole-exome sequencing in 2 sibs from a Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: Whole-exome sequencing was used in the 2 siblings with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.

checks.claim: The 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia reported by Dasouki et al. (2013) were homozygous for a c.112C-T transition in the THPO gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: The siblings are homozygous for c.112C>T. A C-to-T change is a transition.

checks.claim: The THPO c.112C-T transition results in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation encodes an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38
checks.explanation: The paper states the substitution is R38C.

checks.claim: The THPO R38C substitution is designated R17C when the 21-amino acid signal peptide is excluded.
checks.evidence_quote: an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38 or residue 17 excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide
checks.explanation: The paper gives the R17C numbering for when the signal peptide is excluded.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) identified a homozygous arg99-to-trp (R99W) mutation in the THPO gene in patients with inherited bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) identified a homozygous arg99-to-trp (R99W) mutation in the THPO gene in patients with inherited bone marrow failure.
checks.evidence_quote: THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families
checks.explanation: The abstract reports R99W as homozygous in the affected children of two families.
